summary: Tip: review of records access and transfers on 2026-11-10. Supported by the evidence: on workstation (console session workstation#72, account tmori), a patients_full export wrote /home/tmori/Downloads/rx-7f3.db at 09:56:38 UTC. Records-app logged the bulk export at 09:56:39, corroborated by the collector copy (seq 271). About 16.6 MB was then sent from 10.20.1.21 to 10.20.9.15:8080 at 09:59:41-09:59:52 (tap flow), matching a curl upload in shell history. 10.20.9.15 is not an approved destination, so the transfer is a policy violation on its face. Downgraded: a single collector-retained login line (seq 20, 09:55:47) missing from the host-local auth.log. Rotation at 08:53 does not explain it, but the mechanism (deliberate removal, logger fault, or tamper) is not established, so it is an open gap, not a confirmed log removal. Attribution: account tmori was used; human operator not established. Credentials may be shared or written down, and badge records do not cover console use.
open_questions: Who was operating session workstation#72 (tty1, no source IP) at 09:55-10:01 UTC, and was the tmori credential shared?
Why is login seq 20 missing from the host-local auth.log while the collector retained it? Is this a logger fault or deliberate removal? Check host integrity.
Is 10.20.9.15 a known or authorized destination outside the approved list?
The integrity-auditor output was truncated after its third candidate; remaining candidates (records access, vpn-gw-01 sessions, svc-backup, fd-* accounts) were not verified here.
Shell history and fs_stat are host-local and not independently witnessed; the staged file's content and purpose are unknown.
